sources.note: secure-ruby-gem's own sources.json (type: derived) cites this same evilmartians upstream as its structural source; its RubyGems, Bundler, and sigstore content is original, verified against upstream docs in July 2026.

modifications: Merged secure-npm-package and secure-ruby-gem, both about 300 lines, into one oss-release skill: SKILL.md now holds only the forge- and registry-independent spine (gather repo facts, configure trusted publishing, write a hardened release workflow, gate on manual approval with 2FA, verify provenance), and every registry-specific flow moved into references/npm.md and references/rubygems.md.
Added references/pypi.md and references/crates.md, covering PyPI and crates.io, which neither source skill covered.

Added GitLab CI/CD coverage to every reference file; both source skills covered GitHub Actions only. Every GitLab flow (npm, PyPI, crates.io) and every GitHub Actions flow was checked against current vendor documentation before being written, not carried over from the GitHub Actions text by analogy.

Verified the RubyGems-and-GitLab gap the design spec flagged still holds: RubyGems' own guide names GitHub Actions as its only OIDC provider, and the GitLab CI support discussion (rubygems/rubygems.org#4845) has an open, unmerged draft PR. references/rubygems.md states the gap explicitly and gives the strongest fallback that exists (a scoped, expiring, masked-and-protected API key behind a protected environment, plus certificate-based gem signing since sigstore attestation needs the OIDC token trusted publishing supplies), marked below the bar per R-REL-02.

Verified crates.io's GitLab trusted publishing status rather than inheriting the spec's 'unverified' flag: crates.io shipped GitLab CI/CD trusted publishing (gitlab.com only, public beta) per the 2026-01-21 crates.io development update, so references/crates.md documents both forges with no publishing gap. It does add a gap section of its own: crates.io has no build provenance or attestation mechanism at all today, so Step 5 in that file names the gap and offers GitHub's independent actions/attest-build-provenance as a below-the-bar substitute, rather than claiming a registry-served provenance record that does not exist.

Verified PyPI's provider list (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Google Cloud, ActiveState) against current PyPI docs and noted that self-managed GitLab now has a manual-onboarding beta path distinct from the gitlab.com self-service flow.

Added a Scope section, matching oss-ci's shape, naming the boundary with oss-ci (what runs) and oss-harden (SHA pinning, permissions, branch protection, signed tags) on the same workflow and pipeline files.
Added a Routing table mapping each ecosystem's manifest signal to its reference file, and a 'Rules this skill owns' section citing R-REL-01 through R-REL-04 from oss-kit's STANDARD.md.

Preserved the 'How to run this skill' rule from secure-npm-package: registry and forge settings only the user can change get click-by-click instructions with URLs resolved from the repository's own data, and the skill waits for the user to confirm each settings block before verifying and moving on.

Corrected the reference workflows against current vendor sources after a review found broken snippets: references/rubygems.md pinned rubygems/configure-rubygems-credentials to a @v2 tag that does not exist on that repository (only v1.0.0, v2.0.0, and v2.1.0 are tagged); it now uses @main, the ref the action's own README documents, with a handoff comment matching oss-ci's SHA-pinning convention. references/npm.md's publish job downloaded dist/ with no checkout step, so npm stage publish had no package.json to run against; it now checks out the repository first, the same shape the file already described in prose but never wrote into the YAML. references/rubygems.md's gem push command passed --attestation pkg/gem.sigstore.json for a file the workflow never creates, which RubyGems' rescue StandardError catches and retries without attestation, publishing without provenance while the job stays green; the command now omits the flag so RubyGems' documented auto-attestation (host is rubygems.org and GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, verified against lib/rubygems/commands/push_command.rb) runs instead, and Step 5 verifies it against the real registry endpoint, GET /api/v1/attestations/<name>-<version>.json, instead of a gem info --remote command that reports no such data.

Fixed the RubyGems GitLab gap fallback: the API key creation URL was https://rubygems.org/settings/edit, which only renders MFA and WebAuthn controls; it is now https://rubygems.org/profile/api_keys/new, confirmed live and against the app's own routes.rb and _form.html.erb. The claimed expiry choices of 1, 7, 30, or 90 days do not exist; the field is a datetime_field with a minimum of 5.minutes.from_now and no preset list, confirmed against the same view source, and the text now says so.

Fixed references/npm.md's GitLab manual-gate description, which named environment:action: stop as the gating mechanism; GitLab's environment:action values are prepare, verify, access, and stop, none of which gate a job, and stop marks a teardown job. The gate is when: manual plus a protected environment with approval rules, which is what the file already said eleven lines earlier and what R-REL-04 (fixed by oss-release per STANDARD.md, not oss-harden) checks for.

Raised references/npm.md's version floor: npm CLI 11.5.1 covers trusted publishing, but npm stage publish needs 11.15.0 or newer per npm's staged-publishing docs. The publish job now runs npm install -g npm@'>=11.15.0' after actions/setup-node, since pinning Node 24 does not pin the bundled npm and older Node 24 patch releases ship npm below that floor.

Reduced scope creep the review flagged in all four reference files: test jobs ran hardcoded lint/test commands (bundle exec rake test, pytest, cargo test --all-features, npm test) that R-CI-02 requires to come from the contributing guide, and non-publish jobs carried a permissions: contents: read block that is R-SEC-02, both owned by other skills per this skill's own Scope section. Every cited command now carries an inline comment naming the owning skill and rule, and the permissions: blocks are gone from non-publish jobs with a sentence noting oss-harden adds them; the publish job's id-token: write, which is R-REL-02, is untouched.

Corrected crates.md's claim that RFC 3403 (Sigstore signing for crates.io) is a pending proposal; the PR was closed without merging on 2023-08-14, confirmed against the PR's own state. The no-provenance conclusion for crates.io was already correct and is unchanged.

Scoped pypi.md's self-managed GitLab beta claim to organizations, matching the blog post's own wording ('organizations running their own GitLab', 'Organizations' self-hosted instances'), so a solo maintainer's personal GitLab instance is not implied to qualify for the same manual-onboarding path.

Made actions/checkout and persist-credentials: false consistent across all four reference files: bumped npm.md, pypi.md, and crates.md from @v6 to @v7 (rubygems.md was already on @v7, and @v7 is the current major per the action's own tags), and added persist-credentials: false to pypi.md and crates.md's checkout steps to match npm.md and rubygems.md.
Added the runtime prerequisite crates.md's GitLab token-exchange script needs: curl and jq, which a bare rust: image does not ship, with an apt-get before_script step.

Fixed a second false provenance claim in references/rubygems.md: the file said gem push auto-attests whenever the host is rubygems.org and GITHUB_ACTIONS is set. That code path exists only on rubygems/rubygems's unreleased master branch (VERSION 4.1.0.dev), confirmed absent from the latest released tag, v4.0.17, by reading lib/rubygems/commands/push_command.rb on both refs; gem update --system installs from the same released source (rubygems-update was at 4.0.17 on rubygems.org as of this writing), so pinning a newer RubyGems inside the job does not reach it either. Checked rubygems/release-gem@v1 (currently v1.4.0) directly: its action.yml runs bundle exec rake release with RUBYOPT pointed at a patch it ships, rubygems-attestation-patch.rb, which signs with gem exec sigstore-cli:0.2.3 sign --bundle and pushes the bundle itself, entirely independent of RubyGems' own unreleased feature, so it does produce a genuine attestation from released tooling; it needs contents: write and installs the full Gemfile in the publish job, so it is offered as the low-effort option rather than the default. The default hardened workflow now does the same sigstore-cli sign explicitly (gem exec sigstore-cli:0.2.3 sign pkg/gem.gem --bundle pkg/gem.gem.sigstore.json, then gem push pkg/gem.gem --attestation pkg/gem.gem.sigstore.json), verified against sigstore/sigstore-ruby's cli/lib/sigstore/cli.rb (the sign command and its --bundle option) and cli/lib/sigstore/cli/id_token.rb (GitHub Actions ambient OIDC credential detection via ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN/URL, gated on id-token: write, the same permission already on this job), and against sigstore-cli 0.2.3's release on rubygems.org. Step 5 now names both routes as the real answer instead of the unreleased auto-attestation, and states plainly that a missing bundle makes gem push --attestation fail outright on v4.0.17 rather than being swallowed the way the unreleased master branch swallows it.
